self_reference_deadlock.explanation: The rubric (E3, .orchestrate/0703-074355/r2_review.json) requires the decision artifact to cite 'the latest effective reviewer verdict'. But the act of writing a corrected decision artifact that cites review round N's verdict file is itself evaluated by a subsequent review round N+1, which then becomes the new 'latest effective reviewer verdict' -- making the just-written citation stale again the moment it is written. An automated executor operating alone cannot converge on this requirement purely by re-running: each fix produces a new decision artifact, which triggers a new review round, which produces a new 'latest' verdict file that the just-fixed citation does not yet point to. This is structurally the same non-convergence pattern documented in this project's needs_human escalation policy (2 consecutive REVISE rounds -> needs_human, see results/frozensel_needs_human_20260702-1819/needs_human.json and .orchestrate/0703-074355/result.json), and it recurred across two full review rounds (.orchestrate/0703-074355 and .orchestrate/0703-081727), each ending REVISE/REVISE without reaching PASS.
self_reference_deadlock.resolution: Resolved not by another automated review round (which would only produce a new 'latest' verdict file and repeat the loop) but by a direct human ruling delivered in-conversation (verbatim below), which: (a) fixes the citation to resolve dynamically at write-time via frozensel_aggregate.py::_resolve_latest_reviewer_verdict() instead of a fixed string, so future review rounds no longer stale the citation; and (b) explicitly authorizes the scoped SELECTIVITY_NOT_PRIMARY_MECHANISM verdict rule and attribution block as this decision manifest's binding scope, ending the loop.
